answer:
Compute the minimum solid circular shaft diameter d required to satisfy an angle-of-twist limit under pure torsion.
Use N–mm–MPa units throughout.
Shaft length L = 1500 mm.
Material is 6061-T6 aluminum with shear modulus G = 25939.8 MPa.
Applied torque T = 1,000,000 N·mm (10⁶ N·mm).
Angle-of-twist limit φ_allow = 0.75° over the full length L, which must be converted to radians (0.75 × π/180 ≈ 0.01309 rad) before use in the formula.
Use the governing relation φ = TL/(JG) with the polar moment of inertia for a solid circular shaft J = πd⁴/32.
Solve the twist limit φ ≤ φ_allow for the minimum diameter, giving d ≥ [32TL/(πGφ_allow)]^(1/4).
Report the numerical minimum diameter d in mm.
State that the design is stiffness (twist) governed since no allowable shear stress is specified.
As supplementary information, report the resulting maximum torsional shear stress τ = Tc/J = 16T/(πd³) at the design diameter, noting it is not a design constraint.
Note that the general mention of shear loading carries no transverse shear force value and is not part of this sizing computation.
State all assumptions: solid circular cross section, small-deformation linear-elastic behavior, uniform torque along the shaft, one end fixed against twist relative to the other, and no stress concentrations.
Present the governing relations and unit handling clearly in the final answer.
